evidence: Full head-to-toe check at 07:25: no injury, no pain, observations normal. GP reviewed at 11:00 and found no injury. No treatment needed.
summary: E.W. caught her foot on a bath mat while walking to the bathroom with a care worker present and was lowered gently to the floor. No injury or pain. GP reviewed and confirmed no injury or treatment needed.

evidence: Staff called police at 15:30 and reported R.T. missing. Police found R.T. at a bus stop 2 km away at 17:10.
summary: R.T. left the unit through a garden gate propped open by a contractor. Police were called and located him at a bus stop 2km away, cold and confused but unhurt.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: M.K. said "he grabbed me hard last night when I didn't want to get up"
summary: Staff found new bruising on both of M.K.'s forearms. M.K. alleged a care worker grabbed her hard overnight when she refused to get up. GP prescribed pain relief and dressings. Care worker stood down pending investigation.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The safe access log shows one staff member opened it on each of the four days.
summary: J.P.'s daughter reported four cash withdrawals totalling $240 from J.P.'s bank card between 1 and 10 October. The card is kept in the facility safe and the access log shows one staff member opened it on each occasion. Staff member stood down.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The night agency nurse raised both bed rails for D.L. overnight "to stop him wandering". D.L. has no assessment, consent or behaviour support plan for bed rails.
summary: Agency nurse raised both bed rails overnight to prevent wandering without assessment, consent, or behaviour support plan. Rails lowered at 06:00. No injury or distress observed.

evidence: A.N. requires minced and moist meals under her speech pathologist's plan. At lunch she was served a regular-texture roast.
summary: Resident on a minced and moist diet was served a regular-texture roast. She coughed on the first mouthful. Staff removed the meal and an RN assessed her with no distress or treatment needed.
